questions.key_step: Factorise both quadratics; sign of tan decides which root is larger.
questions.justification: Two routine factorisations and one sign decision; short chain with a sign trap.

questions.key_step: Cot-difference identity to telescope with step $\frac{\pi}{6}$.
questions.justification: One standard telescoping device then evaluating $\cot\frac{5\pi}{12}$; familiar to coached students.

questions.key_step: Half-angle tangent substitution, then the $\pm$ of the square root.
questions.justification: Mechanical algebra after a standard substitution; the $\pm$ gives two options. Single concept so no multi-correct floor.

questions.key_step: Shift by $\frac14$ to reveal $\sin\pi y\,(5-2\sin^2\pi y)$, then the window of $x$.
questions.justification: The shift is non-obvious, several identities must be chained exactly, and a numerical answer with an interval-intersection step leaves no option to check against.

questions.key_step: Group terms into $\cos(\alpha-\beta)$ over double angles, then evaluate with sum/product identities.
questions.justification: Pairing idea is not routine, a long exact chain with sign risk, and the final floor needs the value to be located between integers.

questions.key_step: Regroup into $\cos\frac{x}{2}+\sin\frac{x}{2}$, then evaluate with quadrant signs.
questions.justification: Compound-angle regrouping disguised by $\frac{11x}{2}$ and $6x$ plus a quadrant sign; options help verification.

questions.key_step: Cot-telescoping over alternate pairs and cancellation by $\cot(180^\circ-\theta)=-\cot\theta$.
questions.justification: Standard telescoping does not close; the supplementary-angle cancellation is the unfamiliar idea and the answer is numerical.

questions.key_step: $1-2\cos\theta=-\frac{\cos(3\theta/2)}{\cos(\theta/2)}$, telescoping product of five factors with reduction of $\frac{243\pi}{22}$.
questions.justification: Triple-angle telescoping is an uncommon idea; sign bookkeeping through five factors and the final reduction can slip.
